definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese confections with low moisture content and long shelf life, such as {落雁|らくがん}, {金平糖|こんぺいとう}, and {煎餅|せんべい}. Contrasted with {生菓子|なまがし} (fresh, moist sweets). Frequently served with tea, especially in tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}し{菓子|がし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦お{茶|ちゃ}→お茶：00576_ocha⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|だ}した→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: I served dried sweets together with tea.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{老舗|しにせ}→老舗：16152_shinise⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{綺麗|きれい}な{干|ほ}し{菓子|がし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought beautiful dried sweets at a long-established shop in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{薄茶|うすちゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせて→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧{干|ほ}し{菓子|がし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|だ}される→出す：01087_dasu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: At a tea ceremony, dried sweets are often served to go with the thin tea.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧ ("to dry") + ⟦{菓子|かし}→菓子：00191_kashi⟧ ("sweets"); the second element shifts to ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ (rendaku).

CLASSIFICATION:
Japanese confections are broadly divided by moisture content:
- {干|ほ}し{菓子|がし} (≤10% moisture): {落雁|らくがん}, ⟦{金平糖|こんぺいとう}→金平糖：14498_konpeitou⟧, hard candies, dry biscuits — long shelf life
- ⟦{半生菓子|はんなまがし}→半生菓子：28743_hannamagashi⟧ (10–30% moisture): semi-moist sweets
- ⟦{生菓子|なまがし}→生菓子：27039_namagashi⟧ (≥30% moisture): fresh sweets such as ⟦{大福|だいふく}→大福：12173_daifuku⟧ and ⟦{練|ね}り{切|き}り→練り切り：28742_nerikiri⟧ — must be eaten quickly

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干|ほ}し{菓子|がし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: to serve dried sweets
- {干|ほ}し{菓子|がし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ→詰め合わせ：14175_tsumeawase⟧: an assortment of dried sweets (a common gift)
- {薄茶|うすちゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{干|ほ}し{菓子|がし}: dried sweets paired with thin matcha
